hook.text: A restaurant with a line outside seems better than an empty one. You have no other data, but the line convinces you.

buildup.text: Social proof means using other people's behavior as a shortcut for your own decisions.

discovery.text: Hotels that say '75% of guests in this room reused their towels' get far more towel reuse than those that preach.

twist.text: Social proof can mislead. Crowds have run toward danger because everyone followed someone who was also clueless.

climax.text: Before following the crowd, ask: do these people actually know more than me, or are they just guessing too?

punchline.text: Crowds can be wise or blind. Ask before you follow.

quiz.question: When is social proof most dangerous?
options: When the crowd is very large
When the crowd is guessing too and nobody actually has better information
When the behavior is popular on social media
